dateAssessment: The working campaign span is January 25–26, 1730, from the session YAML; no year, month, day or completed overnight is spoken in this source. The time extraction is compatible with that span, with the closing boundary open. Melusa’s stationary late-afternoon light is a local reading, not a civil watch or day counter; the noon view through the gash is another local clock. The gong and dinner suggest a local dusk/sleep period without an actual sunset. Elapsed-only rows retain open watches. The one-hour conversation and dinner receive one short-rest credit; the intended long rest is explicitly uncompleted at cutoff. The dated campaign record supplies the recording-date discrepancy and the competing scout ordering flagged above.

watches.summary: Kalima pauses about a minute before the escape; no clock is established.
The tunnel crawl takes about ten minutes before the party reaches the cliff.
Late-afternoon light remains fixed throughout the village scenes.
About 45 minutes pass from the fey’s dispatch to the conversation in the house.
About an hour talking and dining earns one short rest; Ekko scouts during the conversation.
Noon-like shadows appear across the gash while Melusa keeps its stationary afternoon light.
The gong rings during dinner, marking local sleep time without a sunset.
Two ten-minute castings surround roughly ten minutes of tower observation after Ekko’s return.
The party attempts a long rest; completion and next-day waking remain explicitly deferred.
